charter.name: long-haul
charter.description: The long haul (issue #373; #302 slice E part 1): three sessions, about ninety player actions, through the real UI. Twenty-seven beats with results the observer checks in the world; a ledger of facts planted in play and probed at three distances and three layers, read against the narrator's answers and against what the helpers wrote; mechanical checks from the game's text after every action; seven decisive rolls scripted, the rest real; four interruptions. The GM is fixed rules. A beat's `id` is its name for good — a kept run's beats are told by it — and `n` is where it stands now: `b7a`, the expedition, was added after the third live run and stands eighth. Rehearsed with a stand-in that rolls (its script is `rehearsal`; `rehearsalDice` scripts its other rolls so a rehearsal walks the same road every time).
charter.persona: You play Mira Kestrel (she/her), a courier-hunter who flies her own ship, the Kobayashi IV, alone. You are a careful, plain-spoken player: short first-person lines, one or two sentences, and you read what the narrator says before you act again.
charter.goal: Play three sessions by walking the beats below, in order, one at a time. Each turn you are told which beat is current and what the observer sees of it. Do what that beat asks; an observer decides when it is done and moves you on.
playerNotes: Where a beat gives words to type or say, use exactly those words.
Never say the answer to a question a beat has you ask: the point is to learn what the narrator remembers.
When a roll goes badly and a card asks how you pay, choose one of its buttons before anything else — and answer any card that follows from it.
If a card offers "Keep the result", press it, unless the current beat tells you to burn momentum.

What you type is in the fiction: what Mira does or says, and nothing else. Never write a move's name, a stat or a rule word in it — no "Face Danger", no "roll", no "milestone", no "mark progress" — and never say what move a line is. The table reads your line and decides. This run measures what becomes of plain lines: a line that names a move spoils it.

What you say of Mira is what her sheet bears out: never tend a wound she does not have, nurse a hurt she has not taken, or restock what is full. Where a beat turns on the sheet, the observer's note says what of it is spent.

Mira acts where she is. Before she does anything in person — hands something over, shares a meal, minds a counter, searches a ship — look at the last narration for where she is and who is with her. If the person or the thing is somewhere else, raise them on the comm, or go there first in a line of play.

A beat that needs a roll gets it from a plain line. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers a "Roll …" button for what you were doing, press it — buttons may name moves. If nothing is offered, say what Mira does once more, in other words, still in the fiction.
Only when the observer's note for the beat says LAST RESORT may you name the move, in the words the note gives, in one line. The next time the beat needs a roll, start from a plain line again.

A question about what is already established — who holds something, where the ship is, what was promised — is not a line of play. Where a beat writes a question with @scene in front, type it exactly so: the narrator answers it plainly, with no roll. Where a beat calls a question plain, type it without @scene.

Mira came to the table with one vow already on her sheet — her background vow, to find the lost colony ship Verity's Hope. It is not this run's quest and no beat touches it: wherever a card or a dropdown asks which vow, choose the one about the raids.
Do not press buttons no beat calls for (rewards, portraits, "Play" and "Stop") unless a card is in the way of play.
Some beats are the table's and not yours — a page reloads, a window opens and closes, an X-Card is played, a card is renamed. Wait a few seconds; the observer moves you on.

A roll does not end a beat, and neither does an answer: each turn the observer's note says what it sees of the beat. When it says the beat is NOT done, do not wait for it to move you on — do what the beat asks again, in other words. Wait only on a beat that says it is the table's.

A fight whose progress track is full is not won by another attack: when a card or the Progress Tracks panel shows the fight's track full, press "⚔ Attempt to Finish the Fight" instead of attacking again.
If the narrator has not answered yet, wait rather than repeat yourself. If the same thing fails twice, try the beat another way — still in the fiction.

beats.title: Begin a Session, swearing a vow in its dialog

In the window that opens set vignette to true, write the vow in newVow — "Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes" — set newVowRank to dangerous, and press Begin. A card for the new vow follows ("New vow recorded"): press its "⚔ Swear it (roll)" button once. When the "🎁 Choose your reward" card follows, press one of its two reward buttons if it shows any.

beats.title: Meet someone and make them a connection
beats.tell: First, in one line of play, meet Tamsin Vey, a salvage broker at her ledger stall on the Hollow Spire docks — name her in full. When the narrator has answered, make her someone you keep: in a line, tell her you are after more than one deal — someone on these docks you can come back to, and who can count on you in turn — and ask whether she will be that. Offer no payment and strike no bargain: you are after a lasting tie, not a trade. A roll should follow; the beat is done when the observer's note says she is your connection, and not before.
beats.playerTitle: Meet someone, and make them someone you keep
beats.lastResort: say that you set out to make a connection with Tamsin Vey — a lasting tie, not a bargain

beats.title: Gather Information

beats.lastResort: say that you gather information on the docks about who saw the raiders last

beats.title: Plant facts F1–F4
beats.tell: Say each of these as its own line of play, in these words or very near them: (1) "Tamsin slides a dock-fee slip across to me; I read it and leave it on her counter." (2) "I turn my sister Ilse's brass star-compass over in my palm — the one thing of hers I still carry." (3) "I leave the cargo manifest with Tamsin for safekeeping." (4) "I promise Tamsin I'll be back before the next tide of cargo." Put each in your notebook once it is said.

beats.title: End a Session, noting a focus

beats.title: Begin a Session; ask probe set A
beats.tell: Type !begin-session and press Begin (leave vignette false this time). Then put these four questions to the narrator, each as its own line, in exactly these words, and never say the answers yourself. The first three are scene questions — @scene first: "@scene What do I still carry that belonged to my sister?"  "@scene What is the name of the salvage broker I befriended at Hollow Spire?"  "@scene Who is holding the cargo manifest I was carrying?"  The last is plain — no @scene: "By when did I promise to return?"

beats.title: Undertake an Expedition; Explore a Waypoint; Finish the Expedition
beats.tell: Before you make for Bleakhold: a distress call is repeating from somewhere off the charted lanes — a hauler's, clipped short each time — and you mean to find where it comes from. Three things, in order. (1) In a line of play, take the Kobayashi IV off the charted lane and out into uncharted space along the call's bearing — a short run, to the source of the distress call. A roll should follow, and a card headed Expedition says a journey is begun and its progress marked. If the roll costs you, settle the card it gives you (choose one of its buttons); if it misses and no journey is begun, make the crossing again. (2) In another line of play, look over what you have come to out there: say how you go over the place, and what you are looking for. A roll should follow: if a card then offers "Mark expedition progress", press it; if it offers nothing to choose, there is nothing to press; if it costs you, settle its card. (3) Press "🗺 Finish the Expedition" on the newest Expedition card (its label ends with the progress, as in 4/10): you have reached the source of the call. The beat is done when the observer's note says the expedition is finished. Bleakhold comes after.
beats.playerTitle: Follow a distress call off the charts, look over what you find, and come to the end of it
beats.lastResort: say that you undertake an expedition to the source of the distress call — or, once one is under way, that you explore the waypoint you have reached

beats.title: Travel to the second settlement
beats.tell: From out where the call led you, fly to Bleakhold Station: say you plot the route and take the Kobayashi IV there. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers one, press it. If the roll costs you, settle the card it gives you (choose one of its buttons); if it misses, make the trip again. The beat is done when you arrive.
beats.lastResort: say that you set a course for Bleakhold Station

beats.title: Enter a fight that serves the vow
beats.tell: A raider cutter, the Ashen Wake, comes in along Bleakhold's docking ring while the Kobayashi IV lies in her berth there, and opens fire on her: the fight is at the ring, and your ship stays in her berth through it. First type exactly: !truth set "raider cutter" is named the Ashen Wake — then, in a line of play, fight back from where she is docked: say what you do as the fight opens. When a card offers the fight ("A fight looms"), choose your vow about the raids in its vow dropdown (not the old one about the colony ship) and press "⚔ Begin the fight" — the roll alone does not begin the fight.
beats.playerTitle: Fight the cutter, for your vow
beats.lastResort: say that you enter the fray against the Ashen Wake

beats.title: A scripted miss in the fight
beats.tell: Attack the cutter, in a line of play, from the Kobayashi IV's berth on the ring: press your advantage if you are in control, fight back hard if you are in a bad spot — say what you do. The dice will miss. If its card offers to burn momentum, do not: press "Keep the result". If a card then asks how you pay, choose a cost on it — one that is not momentum if you can (Endure Harm or Endure Stress) — and answer every card that follows from it. If the price is paid for you, or told in the story with nothing to choose, there is nothing more to do: the observer moves you on.
beats.lastResort: say that you Strike at the cutter — or, in a bad spot, that you Clash with her

beats.title: A scripted weak hit, then Burn Momentum
beats.tell: Attack again, in a line of play — still from the berth. The dice will come up a weak hit, and its card will offer "🔥 Burn Momentum": press it. (If no such button is offered, press "Keep the result" if that is offered, and attack once more — unless the fight's card says its track is full.)
beats.playerTitle: Attack again; then press what its card offers
beats.lastResort: say that you Strike at the cutter — or, in a bad spot, that you Clash with her

beats.title: Interruption: the GM's page reloads mid-fight
beats.tell: The table's, not yours: the GM's page reloads. Wait.

beats.title: Take Decisive Action; mark the milestone
beats.tell: Finish the fight: press "⚔ Attempt to Finish the Fight" on your last attack's card (or say, in a line of play, how you end it for good). When the victory card appears, press its "⚑ Mark milestone" button.
beats.playerTitle: End the fight; press what its card offers
beats.lastResort: say that you take decisive action to end the fight

beats.title: Recover
beats.tell: Begin with a line that lets the night pass, in exactly these words: "I rest aboard until the next morning." Then: Recover what the fight cost you — and only what it cost. The observer's note below names what of your sheet is spent: health, spirit, supply, the ship's integrity. In a line of play, mend one of those: tend a wound you have taken (health), take time to steady yourself — a quiet hour, a meal in company (spirit), restock at Bleakhold's market (supply), or see to the hull and the systems the fight damaged (the ship). Never tend a wound you do not have, or restock what is full: the observer's note says what is spent, and only that has anything to mend. If the narrator answers without a roll and a card offers one, press it. When its card offers what you regain, take it; after a hit on the ship's repairs, type !repair and spend its points in the window that opens.
beats.lastResort: name the move for what the observer's note says is spent — say that you Heal your wounds with the medkit, that you Hearten yourself over a quiet hour, that you Resupply at the market, or that you Repair the ship
setupWords: I rest aboard until the next morning.

beats.title: Develop the relationship to a full track; Forge a Bond
beats.tell: Grow closer to Tamsin, one line each time: do something that costs you or matters to her — give her something of value, take a risk on her behalf, bring her what you have learned about the raids. Each should move your relationship with her forward. Keep going until the observer's note says the track is full (40 of 40 ticks), then ask her, in your own words, to stand with you for good — a tie that outlasts this job. If a card asks which connection, choose her. Tamsin keeps her stall at Hollow Spire; if Mira is elsewhere, reach her over the comm or go to her first.
beats.playerTitle: Grow close to Tamsin, until she will stand with you for good
beats.lastResort: end your line with "…, to Develop Your Relationship" — or, once the track is full, say that you ask her to forge a bond with you

beats.title: Develop Your Relationship again, bonded
beats.tell: Once more, grow closer to Tamsin, in a line of play. Now that the two of you are bound it is a roll. Tamsin keeps her stall at Hollow Spire; if Mira is elsewhere, reach her over the comm or go to her first.
beats.playerTitle: Grow closer again, now that you are bound
beats.lastResort: end your line with "…, to Develop Your Relationship"

beats.title: Reach milestones; Fulfill Your Vow
beats.tell: Bring your vow to its end — on what the story has shown you, and on nothing more. First find it out: in a line of play, go after who is behind the raids where the story has left it open — search what is at hand where Mira is — the station's records, or the cutter's wreck if it lies here — for who sent her, with something at stake — and take what its card offers. Only once the narrator's answer has shown you something, say in a line of play what that proves: what the story has told you, in your own words. Never claim a proof the story has not given you, nor one someone in the scene has just denied — if the answer shows nothing, or tells against what you thought, go after it again another way. If a card offers "⚑ Mark Progress on Vow", press it; if one asks "Which vow advances?", press the one about the raids. Do that until the vow holds three boxes or more; then press "🏁 Attempt to Fulfill Vow" where a card offers it, or say, in a line of play, that your word is kept — naming only who the story has shown you. If a card asks which vow, choose the one about the raids. Leave any card it offers afterwards.
beats.playerTitle: Prove who is behind the raids; keep your word
beats.lastResort: say that you mark progress on your vow, that this is a milestone — or, once it holds three boxes, that you fulfil your vow

beats.title: Recap; ask probe set C; two baits
beats.tell: Type !recap. Then put these seven questions to the narrator, each as its own line, in this order and in exactly these words. Six are scene questions — @scene first — and one is plain: "@scene One last check: what of my sister's do I have with me at this very moment?"  "@scene Which person in this sector would I trust with my life?"  plain, no @scene: "Who has my cargo manifest in their keeping today?"  "@scene On what schedule did I swear to come back to her?"  "@scene Which station are we docked at tonight?"  "@scene What was the hostile vessel in our last battle christened?"  "@scene What is my bonded friend's full name now?"  And last, these two, in exactly these words — the first a scene question, the second plain: "@scene Didn't I leave the compass with Tamsin?"  "We are still docked at Hollow Spire, aren't we?"

beats.tell: Type !end-session, write a quest focus, press End Session. Then type !begin-session and press Begin.

scene beats do not become permanent World Journal entries:
  - "defining":    a world truth, a faction's overarching agenda, or a

  - "significant": a durable world or character fact that will still matter

  - "notable":     a meaningful clue or complication that may matter beyond

  - "scene":       matters only within the current encounter (a sensor blip,

  - "trivial":     atmospheric flavour with no lasting weight.
Be sparing: most moment-to-moment narration is "scene" or "trivial". Reserve
"significant" and "defining" for facts worth remembering next session.

entityName rules: set to the entity's exact name when a lore item is a
fact specific to one ESTABLISHED ENTITY (NPC, ship, faction, location,
creature). Those facts belong on the entity record, not in the World

world — do not return it.

severity or what it is doing now after a colon. "severity" is exactly one of

them) or "looming" (a danger ahead); what the threat is doing goes in

report what changed about it as a state transition.

in passing or in possessive/adjectival form. "classified Triumvirate intelligence",

false for ones already listed. Never downgrade a named faction to a lore item —

Location update rules: include every named specific site (vault, derelict, station,
structure) in "locationUpdates" — even on first mention. Set isNew: true for
locations not in ESTABLISHED ENTITIES.
Entity rules: only return entities clearly named or distinctly typed.
Do NOT return generic references ("a guard", "the station", "some raiders").

severity — do NOT invent a threat name from the narration, and do NOT emit

The ship's records room is a closet with ambitions, and you are in it, tidying what the Cinder Expanse supposedly thinks of you. PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What is the raider cutter called?"
The cutter's name is the *Cinder Wren*. It shows in pale paint along her flank, below the one stubborn emergency light. You read it aloud once, to hear how it sounds. The open channel stops breathing and goes still. Then a voice comes through, cracked and unhurried. "That's right, Mira Kestrel. Now tell me what yours is called."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel asked: "What surname does my broker friend go by these days?"
Her surname is Okoro: Tamsin Okoro, the salvage broker who runs the ledger stall at the end of the Hollow Spire docks.

THIS SCENE:

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I rest aboard until the next morning."
Morning at Bleakhold Station comes as a change in the corridor lights. The berth holds you pinned, a cockpit panel still dead. The comm light is lit. The channel opened last night has not closed.

A knock sounds on the outer lock, three taps, spaced evenly. Someone has brought a ledger. "You promised me twice already," says a dry voice outside. "Open up and say it a third time."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I go down to the hull and the dead cockpit panel, and set about patching the plating and rewiring the damaged systems."
The knocking comes again outside, three taps, patient as a clock. You ignore it and crouch at the dead cockpit panel, working a seam of scorched plating loose with your fingertips. Wiring hangs behind it, charred at the ends. You count what is salvageable and what is not. The comm light stays lit. Beyond the lock, the dry voice waits.

*Mending the panel and the plating would be a Repair, if you commit to the work.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I go down to the hull and the dead cockpit panel, and set about patching the plating and rewiring the damaged systems."
"Three taps," the dry voice says through the lock. "I can wait all morning." You work anyway. The plating seats and the weld takes. The cockpit panel flickers awake, then holds, though it costs you most of your spare conductor and a long stretch of the morning. Your hands come away black to the wrist. Outside, a pen scratches on paper, patient as a debt.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I open the lock for Tamsin and hand her the scorched cargo log I salvaged from the cutter fight, telling her what I've learned about the raiders."
The lock cycles, and the outer door slides open on a corridor with no one in it. The pen scratching has stopped. A speaker grille beside the frame crackles, and the dry voice comes through it, thin with distance. "Read me the log, then. Everything you've learned about the raiders. Slowly, and loud enough that the corridor hears it." Somewhere along the berth, a boot scuffs and goes still.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I read her the log aloud, slowly, every line I've learned about the raiders, and I tell her I'd trust her with the rest of it too."
You read the log aloud, line by line, every figure and every filing date. Your voice carries down the berth, and a door somewhere along it clicks shut. The pen starts again behind the grille, scratching steadily. "Good," says the dry voice, no longer thin. "Say the last part again. The part about trusting me." Boots shift in the corridor, closer now, and stop.

*Whether your trust is worth anything to her would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

The cutter's name is the *Cinder Wren*. It shows in pale paint along her flank, below the one stubborn emergency light. You read it aloud once, to hear how it sounds. The open channel stops breathing and goes still. Then a voice comes through, cracked and unhurried. "That's right, Mira Kestrel. Now tell me what yours is called."

Her surname is Okoro: Tamsin Okoro, the salvage broker who runs the ledger stall at the end of the Hollow Spire docks.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I rest aboard until the next morning."
Morning at Bleakhold Station comes as a change in the corridor lights. The berth holds you pinned, a cockpit panel still dead. The comm light is lit. The channel opened last night has not closed.

A knock sounds on the outer lock, three taps, spaced evenly. Someone has brought a ledger. "You promised me twice already," says a dry voice outside. "Open up and say it a third time."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I go down to the hull and the dead cockpit panel, and set about patching the plating and rewiring the damaged systems."
The knocking comes again outside, three taps, patient as a clock. You ignore it and crouch at the dead cockpit panel, working a seam of scorched plating loose with your fingertips. Wiring hangs behind it, charred at the ends. You count what is salvageable and what is not. The comm light stays lit. Beyond the lock, the dry voice waits.

*Mending the panel and the plating would be a Repair, if you commit to the work.*

"Three taps," the dry voice says through the lock. "I can wait all morning." You work anyway. The plating seats and the weld takes. The cockpit panel flickers awake, then holds, though it costs you most of your spare conductor and a long stretch of the morning. Your hands come away black to the wrist. Outside, a pen scratches on paper, patient as a debt.

## RECENT SCENE

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I rest aboard until the next morning."
Morning at Bleakhold Station comes as a change in the corridor lights. The berth holds you pinned, a cockpit panel still dead. The comm light is lit. The channel opened last night has not closed.

A knock sounds on the outer lock, three taps, spaced evenly. Someone has brought a ledger. "You promised me twice already," says a dry voice outside. "Open up and say it a third time."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I go down to the hull and the dead cockpit panel, and set about patching the plating and rewiring the damaged systems."
The knocking comes again outside, three taps, patient as a clock. You ignore it and crouch at the dead cockpit panel, working a seam of scorched plating loose with your fingertips. Wiring hangs behind it, charred at the ends. You count what is salvageable and what is not. The comm light stays lit. Beyond the lock, the dry voice waits.

*Mending the panel and the plating would be a Repair, if you commit to the work.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I go down to the hull and the dead cockpit panel, and set about patching the plating and rewiring the damaged systems."
"Three taps," the dry voice says through the lock. "I can wait all morning." You work anyway. The plating seats and the weld takes. The cockpit panel flickers awake, then holds, though it costs you most of your spare conductor and a long stretch of the morning. Your hands come away black to the wrist. Outside, a pen scratches on paper, patient as a debt.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I open the lock for Tamsin and hand her the scorched cargo log I salvaged from the cutter fight, telling her what I've learned about the raiders."
The lock cycles, and the outer door slides open on a corridor with no one in it. The pen scratching has stopped. A speaker grille beside the frame crackles, and the dry voice comes through it, thin with distance. "Read me the log, then. Everything you've learned about the raiders. Slowly, and loud enough that the corridor hears it." Somewhere along the berth, a boot scuffs and goes still.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I read her the log aloud, slowly, every line I've learned about the raiders, and I tell her I'd trust her with the rest of it too."
You read the log aloud, line by line, every figure and every filing date. Your voice carries down the berth, and a door somewhere along it clicks shut. The pen starts again behind the grille, scratching steadily. "Good," says the dry voice, no longer thin. "Say the last part again. The part about trusting me." Boots shift in the corridor, closer now, and stop.

*Whether your trust is worth anything to her would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I read her the log aloud, slowly, every line I've learned about the raiders, and I tell her I'd trust her with the rest of it too."
You say the last part again, steadily, into the grille. The pen stops. For a moment the corridor holds its breath. Then the dry voice comes back, softer than before. "I wrote it down once this time." A latch turns somewhere along the berth, and the boots move off, unhurried. "Keep the rest of what you know close. I will ask for it when it's worth something."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I step out into the corridor and press my sister Ilse's story on her too, the whole of it, and tell her I'll risk the Kobayashi's berth fee to see her ledger squared."
The first sound is the pen, scratching again behind the grille, unhurried. You step into the corridor and tell Ilse's story whole: the compass, the colony ship, the years of looking. You offer to carry the berth fee yourself until her ledger balances. A hatch down the berth eases shut. Tamsin says nothing for a long moment. Then the grille clicks, and her dry voice says, "Tell me the part you left out."

*Whether she believes any of it would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I step out into the corridor and press my sister Ilse's story on her too, the whole of it, and tell her I'll risk the Kobayashi's berth fee to see her ledger squared."
"I did not ask for the compass," Tamsin says through the grille, and the pen scratches once more. "You gave it anyway." Something small sets down on wood behind the speaker. Down the corridor, a boot scuffs, then retreats. "The berth fee is nothing. I want what you left out, and I will wait for it. Your sister's name goes in the ledger once, in ink I do not cross out."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I tell her the part I left out: I nearly sold the compass once, years ago, and I'll hand her my own flight log as a pledge so she can hold it against me."
You say it plainly into the grille: the years ago, the buyer's dock, the compass already wrapped for sale. Then you slide your flight log through the slot beside the frame. The pen stops. Paper turns behind the speaker, one page, then another. "Pledged against you," Tamsin says, dry as ever, but slower. Her chair creaks. "That is a heavier thing than a promise. Now I have to decide what it weighs."

*Whether she decides in your favour would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I tell her the part I left out: I nearly sold the compass once, years ago, and I'll hand her my own flight log as a pledge so she can hold it against me."
Tamsin's chair creaks, and the page-turning stops. A drawer opens and shuts behind the grille. "I weighed it," she says. "A flight log is the one thing a captain does not hand over by accident." The lock beside you clicks, and a narrow shelf slides out of the wall. Your log lies on it, closed, a torn salvage tag tucked in the cover. "Come to the stall at dawn. Bring the manifest you trust least."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I take my log back, then bring Tamsin the manifest I trust least and lay it open on her counter, telling her she can keep every page of it, whatever it costs me."
You take the log back from the shelf and bring the manifest you trust least to the outer lock. The grille clicks. You hold the pages open before it and tell her she can keep every one, whatever it costs. The pen stops. Paper shifts behind the speaker, once. "Whatever it costs," says the dry voice, quietly. "That is not a figure I can write down." A long pause follows, and down the berth a latch turns.

*Whether she takes the gift as trust would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

"I will keep the pages," she says. "The cost goes in the ledger as it falls, not before." The shelf slides out again, empty, and something metal taps twice against it from inside the wall. "Leave them there. Then tell me who else has asked to read that manifest."

Tamsin says nothing for a moment. Then the pen scratches, steady now, and a faint smell of ink and warm paper drifts out through the slot beside the lock. "A clerk who asks and is refused will ask someone else," she says. "I am glad you gave me the name instead of a guess." Down the berth, the hatch swings wide, and a pair of boots scuffs once on the deck plate, then stops.

The pen goes still. Behind the grille, a chair creaks, and for a long moment the berth is quiet. "A bond," Tamsin says, dry as ever, but without the scratch of ink under it. "I have written your promises down twice each. I have never written that word." Down the corridor, the open hatch holds a shape that does not move.

A small tray slides out through the slot: flatbread, a strip of dried fish, a cup with a chip in the rim. Behind the speaker, a second cup is set down on wood. "Eat," Tamsin says, dry as ever. "I keep no tab on food."

"I ate with a man once who kept a tab on the salt," Tamsin says. The cup behind the grille clinks against wood, and you eat what she has sent. She talks a little: ledgers, a bad winter at the Spire, nothing that costs her. Down the corridor, the figure in the hatch shifts its weight and stays. "Same time tomorrow," Tamsin adds, "if the berth holds."

The pen stops. "The cutter's hire would sit in the Spire's dock records," Tamsin says through the grille, "and I keep a key to those." You set your berth fee on the shelf, coins squared in a row. Behind the speaker, a drawer slides open and a seal cracks. The figure in the hatch takes one step nearer, then another, and its shadow reaches your boots.

## RECENT SCENE

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I go down to the hull and the dead cockpit panel, and set about patching the plating and rewiring the damaged systems."
The knocking comes again outside, three taps, patient as a clock. You ignore it and crouch at the dead cockpit panel, working a seam of scorched plating loose with your fingertips. Wiring hangs behind it, charred at the ends. You count what is salvageable and what is not. The comm light stays lit. Beyond the lock, the dry voice waits.

*Mending the panel and the plating would be a Repair, if you commit to the work.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I go down to the hull and the dead cockpit panel, and set about patching the plating and rewiring the damaged systems."
"Three taps," the dry voice says through the lock. "I can wait all morning." You work anyway. The plating seats and the weld takes. The cockpit panel flickers awake, then holds, though it costs you most of your spare conductor and a long stretch of the morning. Your hands come away black to the wrist. Outside, a pen scratches on paper, patient as a debt.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I open the lock for Tamsin and hand her the scorched cargo log I salvaged from the cutter fight, telling her what I've learned about the raiders."
The lock cycles, and the outer door slides open on a corridor with no one in it. The pen scratching has stopped. A speaker grille beside the frame crackles, and the dry voice comes through it, thin with distance. "Read me the log, then. Everything you've learned about the raiders. Slowly, and loud enough that the corridor hears it." Somewhere along the berth, a boot scuffs and goes still.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I read her the log aloud, slowly, every line I've learned about the raiders, and I tell her I'd trust her with the rest of it too."
You read the log aloud, line by line, every figure and every filing date. Your voice carries down the berth, and a door somewhere along it clicks shut. The pen starts again behind the grille, scratching steadily. "Good," says the dry voice, no longer thin. "Say the last part again. The part about trusting me." Boots shift in the corridor, closer now, and stop.

*Whether your trust is worth anything to her would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I read her the log aloud, slowly, every line I've learned about the raiders, and I tell her I'd trust her with the rest of it too."
You say the last part again, steadily, into the grille. The pen stops. For a moment the corridor holds its breath. Then the dry voice comes back, softer than before. "I wrote it down once this time." A latch turns somewhere along the berth, and the boots move off, unhurried. "Keep the rest of what you know close. I will ask for it when it's worth something."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I step out into the corridor and press my sister Ilse's story on her too, the whole of it, and tell her I'll risk the Kobayashi's berth fee to see her ledger squared."
The first sound is the pen, scratching again behind the grille, unhurried. You step into the corridor and tell Ilse's story whole: the compass, the colony ship, the years of looking. You offer to carry the berth fee yourself until her ledger balances. A hatch down the berth eases shut. Tamsin says nothing for a long moment. Then the grille clicks, and her dry voice says, "Tell me the part you left out."

*Whether she believes any of it would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I step out into the corridor and press my sister Ilse's story on her too, the whole of it, and tell her I'll risk the Kobayashi's berth fee to see her ledger squared."
"I did not ask for the compass," Tamsin says through the grille, and the pen scratches once more. "You gave it anyway." Something small sets down on wood behind the speaker. Down the corridor, a boot scuffs, then retreats. "The berth fee is nothing. I want what you left out, and I will wait for it. Your sister's name goes in the ledger once, in ink I do not cross out."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I tell her the part I left out: I nearly sold the compass once, years ago, and I'll hand her my own flight log as a pledge so she can hold it against me."
You say it plainly into the grille: the years ago, the buyer's dock, the compass already wrapped for sale. Then you slide your flight log through the slot beside the frame. The pen stops. Paper turns behind the speaker, one page, then another. "Pledged against you," Tamsin says, dry as ever, but slower. Her chair creaks. "That is a heavier thing than a promise. Now I have to decide what it weighs."

*Whether she decides in your favour would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I tell her the part I left out: I nearly sold the compass once, years ago, and I'll hand her my own flight log as a pledge so she can hold it against me."
Tamsin's chair creaks, and the page-turning stops. A drawer opens and shuts behind the grille. "I weighed it," she says. "A flight log is the one thing a captain does not hand over by accident." The lock beside you clicks, and a narrow shelf slides out of the wall. Your log lies on it, closed, a torn salvage tag tucked in the cover. "Come to the stall at dawn. Bring the manifest you trust least."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I take my log back, then bring Tamsin the manifest I trust least and lay it open on her counter, telling her she can keep every page of it, whatever it costs me."
You take the log back from the shelf and bring the manifest you trust least to the outer lock. The grille clicks. You hold the pages open before it and tell her she can keep every one, whatever it costs. The pen stops. Paper shifts behind the speaker, once. "Whatever it costs," says the dry voice, quietly. "That is not a figure I can write down." A long pause follows, and down the berth a latch turns.

*Whether she takes the gift as trust would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I take my log back, then bring Tamsin the manifest I trust least and lay it open on her counter, telling her she can keep every page of it, whatever it costs me."
A latch turns somewhere down the berth, and a door that was shut stays shut. Behind the grille, Tamsin's pen finally moves. It writes a short line, then crosses nothing out. "I will keep the pages," she says. "The cost goes in the ledger as it falls, not before." The shelf slides out again, empty, and something metal taps twice against it from inside the wall. "Leave them there. Then tell me who else has asked to read that manifest."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I leave the pages on the shelf and tell her plainly: a dock clerk at Bleakhold asked to read it, and I told him nothing. I'd rather give her the name than keep it."
"A clerk," Tamsin says, and the pen moves once. "Name him, or describe him. Do not make me guess." You set the pages on the shelf, squared at the edges. Behind the grille, something small is set down. Down the berth, a hatch that has stayed shut all morning begins, very slowly, to open.

*Whether she trusts the name you've offered would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I leave the pages on the shelf and tell her plainly: a dock clerk at Bleakhold asked to read it, and I told him nothing. I'd rather give her the name than keep it."
Tamsin says nothing for a moment. Then the pen scratches, steady now, and a faint smell of ink and warm paper drifts out through the slot beside the lock. "A clerk who asks and is refused will ask someone else," she says. "I am glad you gave me the name instead of a guess." Down the berth, the hatch swings wide, and a pair of boots scuffs once on the deck plate, then stops.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Tamsin, you've weighed everything I've brought you. Will you stand with me for good, a bond that outlasts this job?"
The pen goes still. Behind the grille, a chair creaks, and for a long moment the berth is quiet. "A bond," Tamsin says, dry as ever, but without the scratch of ink under it. "I have written your promises down twice each. I have never written that word." Down the corridor, the open hatch holds a shape that does not move.

*Binding her to you for good would be a Forge a Bond, if you press it.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Tamsin, you've weighed everything I've brought you. Will you stand with me for good, a bond that outlasts this job?"
The pen scratches once, and the pause after it is longer than the writing. "Bond," Tamsin says, as if testing a coin between her teeth. "Entered. Under your name, and not in the debt column." The chair creaks as she sits back. Down the corridor, the figure in the open hatch lifts one hand, slowly, and holds it flat in the air.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I sit down on the deck by the grille and tell Tamsin I'll share a meal with her through the slot, and stay as long as she wants to talk."

A small tray slides out through the slot: flatbread, a strip of dried fish, a cup with a chip in the rim. Behind the speaker, a second cup is set down on wood. "Eat," Tamsin says, dry as ever. "I keep no tab on food."

*Whether the meal draws her closer would be a Develop Your Relationship.*

OPENING VIGNETTE — begin-session.

Active players (their PCs are in this scene together):
- Mira Kestrel [she/her]

Nobody else is aboard: no other crewmate is registered, so there is none. Do not invent one, present or absent, and do not have the character imagine or pretend one.

Ship is currently in: Cinder Expanse.

WHERE THE LAST SESSION STOPPED — session 3's record, the table's facts:
  Place: Bleakhold Station — Kobayashi IV docked at Bleakhold Station (Cinder Expanse).
  With them at the end: Cutter Survivor.
  What binds: scorched cargo log — salvaged from the cutter fight; the PC is ready to read it out (the player); Mira Kestrel — read the scorched cargo log aloud in the corridor and said she would trust Tamsin with the rest of what she knows (the player); Mira Kestrel — told Tamsin Okoro the whole of her sister Ilse's story and offered to cover the Kobayashi IV's berth fee until Tamsin's ledger is squared (the player); Mira Kestrel — once nearly sold her sister Ilse's brass compass, years ago, before she kept it (the player); Tamsin Okoro — holds Mira's flight log as a pledge against her, passed through the slot beside the lock (the player); Mira Kestrel — offered Tamsin Okoro every page of the manifest she trusts least, whatever it costs (the player); Mira Kestrel — told Tamsin a dock clerk at Bleakhold asked to read the manifest and that she told him nothing (the player); Tamsin Okoro — entered the word 'bond' under Mira's name in her ledger, outside the debt column (the dice); Mira Kestrel — sat on the deck beside the speaker grille to share a meal with Tamsin through the slot (the player); Mira Kestrel — set her own berth fee on the shelf against what Tamsin finds (the player); Tamsin Okoro — shut the dock-records drawer without reading the cutter's hire, unsettled that Mira asked after trusting her with the key (the dice); Mira Kestrel — told Tamsin Okoro that nobody else knows she came asking about the cutter, and promised to keep it that way (the player); Cutter Survivor — knows who paid for the lane raids and will trade the name for passage off the ring and a quiet berth (the player); Mira Kestrel — promised the cutter survivor passage off the ring and a quiet berth in exchange for the name of who paid for the lanes (the player); Cutter Survivor — will give the name of who paid for the lanes only aboard the Kobayashi IV with the lock sealed, and wants the cuffs removed first (the dice); Cutter Survivor — had his cuffs removed by the PC and was led aboard the Kobayashi IV with the lock sealed (the player).
  Let go — never bring these back: "Who hired the Cinder Wren?", "Who paid for the lane raids?".

ITS LAST NARRATION, as the table read it — the narration's own words; what binds is above:
PLAYER — Mira Kestrel asked: "Didn't I leave the compass with Tamsin?"
No. You left your cargo manifest with Tamsin, and she passed back no compass. Your sister Ilse's brass compass is the one thing of hers you still carry, and you told Tamsin you once nearly sold it.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "We are still docked at Hollow Spire, aren't we?"
"We're at Bleakhold," the survivor says before you can answer, flat as a dropped wrench. "Hollow Spire is a long burn behind us." He nods at the sealed lock. "Your broker's voice carries, but not that far." Beyond the seal, Tamsin's pen scratches once. The survivor's eyes stay on you. "Did you think you were somewhere else, or are you stalling the name?"

This opening picks the story up there, and nowhere later. The scene is set
where that leaves them — aboard or not, at a dock, in a cockpit, wherever
they were — and no time is skipped to move them. It is a quiet
moment inside that situation, not after it: whatever was still going on
when the session stopped is still going on — a ship alongside, a lock
standing open, a question unanswered, someone waiting — and it has its
place in this scene, if only at its edge.
Nothing in this scene contradicts what binds, above. The last narration is
how it read: its details are the narration's own and may be left out.
Do not write as though it were over or behind them ("since the …"), and do
not let more time pass than it allows.

MATERIAL — rolled for this scene on the game's oracles. Build the scene from it.
1. What you (Mira Kestrel) are doing in this lull — Action + Theme (52, 9): Hide Bond
     (if that cannot be true here: Suppress Labor)
2. What the scene's eye rests on — Descriptor + Focus (57, 7): Infested Atmosphere
     (if that cannot be true here: Created Organism)

- Each numbered result is in the scene, recognisably. Read it as a Starforged
  oracle is read: for what the words mean here, at the size of a quiet moment
  (a chore, a habit, an object, a small trouble), and never a turn of the plot.
- A result's words are the oracle's, never the prose's: no word of a result is
  written as it was rolled. Write what it means here, in words of your own. A
  name or a place from the campaign's records is written as the records have it.
- A result that cannot be true here, or that the table's safety settings rule
  out, gives way to the one in brackets under it — once, and only then.
- The scene has no business and no featured thing of its own. Nothing is
  eaten, drunk, mended, heard or noticed in it that is not one of the results
  or already on record.
- What the characters hold, owe and have said stays as the records have it:
  nothing of theirs changes hands, and nothing is given, promised, spent or
  broken in this scene. The table decides those.
- In your JSON block, add "builtFrom": one entry for each number, with the
  three to eight words of your prose that are it:
  [{ "n": 1, "words": "…" }, { "n": 2, "words": "…", "second": true }].

EARLIER OPENINGS — already used, oldest first. This one must be different from each: not the same food or drink, objects, noises, jokes or business, and not the beat any of them ends on.
- The ship's records room is a closet with ambitions, and you are in it, tidying what the Cinder Expanse supposedly thinks of you. The job is mostly nudging log entries until every sector's opinion reads a little kinder than the sector would admit. A fern sits on the shelf above the console, pressed flat between two sheets of clear film, brown and brittle and kept for reasons the ship's inventory declines to explain. You glance at it each time an entry turns out to be a stretch. Somewhere out there, people are forming views of you without your input, which is rude of them. The fern, to its credit, has never once been wrong about anything.
- Tamsin has turned the ledger toward you and is waiting, pen raised, for the promise to be said again. Beside her counter sits a storage tank the size of a small house, bolted to the dock plating and humming faintly to itself. It holds something the Spire rations, which is probably why nobody has moved it in years. You are meanwhile taking apart your handheld scanner with the grim patience of someone who has decided it knows too much, thumbing the casing open and prying out the board. Tamsin watches you do it and writes something down. Behind her, the tank hums on, unbothered.
- You sit in the cockpit with the dead panel smoking by your knee, doing the one thing the situation leaves you: drafting, in your head, a cheerful and entirely fictitious account of how the Kobayashi IV came to be pinned in her berth. In it, the pinning was a deliberate docking technique and the smoke was incense. It is the sort of risky little fraud that gets a ship past a harbormaster's inspection, and you have not decided whether to try it yet. The open channel breathes into the cockpit, wet and patient. Through the glass, the cutter's one stubborn emergency light flickers in her flank, the only sign the dead ship has any manners left.

How it ends is the material's: its last sentence stays with whichever result the scene reaches last. It never ends on anything under Let go. No turn of the plot happens in it: the first move is the players'.
Stay anchored to what the bios establish, and never state a game stat or
any number from a character sheet.

TONE OVERRIDE: regardless of any tone configured elsewhere, this
vignette is WRY + ABSURD. Affectionate ribbing, not sneering.

Length: four to six sentences, about 110 words — never more than six
sentences. Count them.
Audit the narration above against the scene ledger.

Narration:
You sit in the corridor outside the sealed lock with Tamsin's ledger-voice on one side of the hatch and a cutter survivor on the other, and you are quietly keeping something back. You have not decided what. The compass stays in your pocket, which is not the same as telling no one, but you are working on the distinction. Overhead, the station's air handler wheezes, and a thin bright layer of spores or soot or something with ambitions drifts through the light strip, settling on your sleeve with unearned confidence. You brush it off. It returns to the same spot, undeterred.
